svg.title: Jing-Zhang City Completeness: 10 AI+ Scenario Cards
svg.desc: Ten AI+ scenario cards showing users, place, problem, AI enhancement, non-AI baseline, exit path, and validation evidence.
svg.text: Jing-Zhang City Completeness v0.5 | 10 AI+ Scenario Cards
Shared contract: real problem first · AI is optional enhancement · keep a non-AI baseline · human takeover · stoppable/exit-ready · evidence decides scaling

g.text: SCN-01
Controlled low-speed robot testing
Place/users: auditable Zhongzhiyuan test zone | R&D teams, park users
Problem: embodied systems need safety, boundary, and takeover validation before real deployment
AI: low-speed navigation/avoidance/tasks under route, time, and speed limits
Baseline/exit: ordinary public routes stay open; anomaly → human takeover and test stop
Evidence: takeover rate, near misses, boundary breaches, public-route continuity after shutdown
SCN-02
Shared research equipment and compute
Place/users: Zhongzhiyuan research-service node | universities, startups, researchers
Problem: fragmented equipment/compute information and opaque booking/capacity boundaries
AI: demand matching, scheduling advice, capacity alerts; never grants access automatically
Baseline/exit: human desk and conventional booking remain; disputes go to human confirmation
Evidence: wait time, human reassignment rate, capacity conflicts, no-account booking access
SCN-03
University result → urban problem translation
Place/users: university—Zhongzhiyuan—community interface | researchers, services, residents
Problem: technology outputs are hard to convert into testable city problems and responsibilities
AI: classify problems, summarize evidence, match pilot candidates; humans decide projects
Baseline/exit: public issue list, human review, paper/offline participation remain available
Evidence: issue closure, human rejection, provenance coverage, resident-feedback coverage
SCN-04
Shuangfen Fortress accessibility assistant
Place/users: AI Origin Community | older adults, families, disabled users, visitors
Problem: complex routes, service entries, and temporary barriers reduce accessibility
AI: accessible-route guidance, service navigation, temporary-barrier alerts
Baseline/exit: physical wayfinding, staffed help, continuous accessible infrastructure come first
Evidence: route continuity, help response, misguidance rate, access without a smartphone
SCN-05
Voluntary household robot testing
Place/users: opt-in home/public mock-up | families, carers, R&D teams
Problem: home tests involve privacy, child/elder safety, and service continuity after exit
AI: voluntary task support with scenario consent, minimal data, visible status indicators
Baseline/exit: refusal never removes rights; one-step stop + human/conventional alternative
Evidence: exit recovery time, deletion confirmation, human takeover, incident/complaint record
SCN-06
Community shared-space scheduling
Place/users: community commons/shared rooms | residents, groups, service staff
Problem: booking conflicts, displacement of weaker groups, opaque operations
AI: cluster demand, flag conflicts, suggest low-use slots; never auto-cancels bookings
Baseline/exit: staffed ledger and walk-up desk; core public hours cannot become algorithmic paywalls
Evidence: conflict rate, staffed coverage, group fairness, free-public-hour availability
SCN-07
Multilingual Jing-Zhang heritage guide
Place/users: heritage park and civic nodes | residents, students, international visitors
Problem: history is hard to access across languages and AI can invent unsourced narratives
AI: multilingual Q&A and tailored routes using traceable source material only
Baseline/exit: physical labels, human guides, fixed multilingual text remain readable
Evidence: source-hit rate, correction rate, language coverage, offline/no-account access
SCN-08
Complex transfer and walking assistance
Place/users: Dazhongsi/southern station-city interface | commuters, visitors, disabled users
Problem: transfer paths, closures, and accessible detours are difficult to synchronize
AI: route explanation, crowd alerts, accessible alternatives; no control over transport systems
Baseline/exit: physical wayfinding, staff, and statutory accessible routes remain primary
Evidence: wrong-route rate, transfer time, accessible-route success, staffed-help demand
SCN-09
Time-limited AI-native retail pilot
Place/users: Dazhongsi/scenario nodes | startups, customers, neighboring ordinary businesses
Problem: new formats need market evidence without permanent public-resource lock-in
AI: pilot services, demand analysis, operational assistance within time/space/data limits
Baseline/exit: ordinary payment/service access; expiry review, remove and restore if thresholds fail
Evidence: trial conversion, complaints/refunds, exit restoration cost, public-space impact
SCN-10
C7 City Completeness inspection assistant
Place/users: overall design area | planning team, operators, public participants
Problem: iterations can chase tech novelty while missing ordinary capabilities and evidence gaps
AI: flag C7 gaps, evidence, conflicts, unresolved items; never replaces professional judgment
Baseline/exit: human checklist, public matrices, professional review remain final authority
Evidence: gap closure, human override, provenance coverage, public-question closure

svg.text: A scenario moves beyond limited testing only when safety, public interest, privacy, non-AI baseline, and maintenance responsibility all pass; any red-line trigger permits shutdown and restoration of ordinary city service.
All KPIs are concept-stage validation directions, not measured performance or government commitments.
